title: WAL commit-path: widen group-commit window and writer flush batch
configuration_cause: commit_delay=100us with commit_siblings=2 and wal_writer_flush_after=0 leaves the group-commit window too narrow and the writer flushing per-write, so WAL syncs are not coalesced; wal_waiting_backends.max=1 and sync_average_ms=0.137 persist across all rounds.
mechanism: WAL sync latency is not the dominant cost (sync_average_ms 0.137, write 0.026, host_io stalls 0), but a persistent wal_wait anomaly shows occasional commit-path queueing. The mandatory wal_commit_path bundle is actionable only on wal_writer_flush_after, commit_delay and commit_siblings (wal_buffers, wal_writer_delay, wal_compression are non-actionable at incumbent). Widening the group-commit collection window to 500us and raising the activation threshold to 3 lets the 5 terminals' commits coalesce into fewer fsyncs, while a 256-block (2MB) writer flush batch stops per-write flushing. This is a bounded amplitude increase over the previously parked r005/r006/r007 values, testing whether larger coalescing reduces the residual wal_wait without adding fixed per-commit stall.
query_effect: GetUserTweets dominates terminal capacity (0.88); reducing commit-path queueing frees a small fraction of terminal time for the read-heavy mix.
expected_tps_effect: Small increase (0.3-1%) if WAL coalescing removes residual commit stalls; neutral if wal_wait is not on the critical path.
expected_latency_effect: InsertTweet p95 may decrease slightly; GetUserTweets p50/p95 essentially unchanged.

predictions.rationale: Wider group-commit window and larger writer flush batch coalesce fsyncs, lowering average sync time.
Fewer distinct syncs reduce backends waiting on WAL.
Freed commit-path capacity raises completed transaction throughput.

alternatives.statement: WAL sync is already cheap (0.137ms) and wal_wait is a rare 1-backend blip; the bundle changes nothing measurable and TPS stays flat.
A 500us commit_delay adds fixed per-commit stall that outweighs coalescing, lowering TPS and raising InsertTweet p95.

why_exceeds_incumbent: Incumbent leaves the group-commit window at 100us and writer flushing per-write (flush_after=0), so the persistent wal_wait anomaly is unaddressed. A coherent larger-amplitude bundle on the three actionable knobs tests whether coalescing removes residual commit-path queueing.

nodes.label: WAL commit-path bundle: commit_delay 500, commit_siblings 3, wal_writer_flush_after 256
Wider group-commit window plus larger writer flush batch coalesce fsyncs

knob_changes.numerical_basis: Widen from 100us to 500us within safe [0,1000]; 5x window to collect 5 terminals' commits, still under 1ms added latency.
Raise from 2 to 3 within safe [0,20]; with 5 terminals, 3 siblings reliably triggers group commit without over-gating.
Set from 0 to 256 (8kB units) within safe [0,1024]; 2MB flush batch reduces writer sync frequency versus per-write flushing.
